relevance_note: Single-patient case report in which NGS 'revealed a nonsense mutation in the tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-induced protein 3 gene, leading to the diagnosis of haploinsufficiency A20 (HA20)'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON and checked spans; no table was transcribed by script. Single-patient case report. Table 1 is a laboratory table whose columns are time points ('On admission', 'On hospital day 2', 'After 9 months'), not patients. Individuals: the index patient (label 'patient', per schema rule for one unnamed patient) and 'her father', who has clinical history but was not genetically tested ('her parents refused'), so he has no variant row. The mother and younger sister are mentioned only in the refused-testing sentence, with no clinical or genetic information, so they have no rows. The other Korean HA20 patient (ref [8]) and the review statistics (89 patients, ref [4]) are not described individually and have no rows. Ambiguities/contradictions: (1) the text says 'The c.547C>T variation of the proband was present in our patient' and the Fig. 1 legend says 'The c.547C>T mutation of the proband was detected in the patient'; it is unclear who 'the proband' is (possibly a previously published proband, refs [4,6,7]); not interpreted, and no re-report recorded. (2) Fig. 1 legend spells the gene 'TNFIP3' while the text prints 'TNFAIP3'; TNFAIP3 recorded. (3) The protein change is printed 'p.Arg183^*' in the body (likely a superscript rendering) and 'p.Arg183*' in the Fig. 1 legend; the legend form is recorded. Zygosity is never stated, so 'not reported'. Age at last evaluation is the age at presentation ('9-year-old'); follow-up continued at least 9 months after colchicine started, but no later age is given. Age at diagnosis not stated. Country 'Korea' comes from the statement that 2 patients including this case were diagnosed in Korea. Vital status 'alive' is inferred from current treatment planning. 'No uveitis' is recorded as an excluded feature, but the checklist item 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' is left 'not reported' under the narrow/broad rule; likewise the father's 'no arthritis' does not exclude 'arthritis or arthralgia'. The anal ulcer was mapped to the checklist item 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation'. Anti-dsDNA IgG (22.6 and 12.8 IU/mL), C3, C4 and other laboratory values are given without interpretation or reference ranges and were not recorded as features. The father's recurrent tonsillitis was not mapped to 'recurrent infections'.

Colchicine was started, and 9 months after treatment, oral and genital ulcers disappeared. However, the fever continued to recur every 3 or 4 months.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: genetic testing: NGS for genes related to periodic fever and autoinflammatory syndromes, performed because features were atypical for PFAPA, revealed a nonsense TNFAIP3 mutation leading to the diagnosis of HA20
span: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) for genes related to periodic fever and autoinflammatory syndromes was conducted to identify a possible genetic disorder.
It revealed a nonsense mutation in the tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-induced protein 3 gene, leading to the diagnosis of haploinsufficiency A20 (HA20)
These features were atypical for PFAPA syndrome; therefore, we performed NGS to identify inflammatory diseases that cause periodic fever.
